title: MetaCan screening label
description: The output contract for one screened work. docs/protocol/rubric.md instructs both machine screeners and both human coders to return exactly this. It did not exist until 2026-07-11 (DEVIATIONS.md D9): the rubric pointed at a file that was not in the repository, and the schema was inlined in the prompts instead. A locked instrument that references a missing file is not locked.

id.description: OpenAlex work ID, bare (W123456789), not the full URL.

tier.description: RETIRED in rubric v3, which replaces it with the multi-label `categories`. These values are retained ONLY so the v1 and v2 label files stay readable; no new screening emits them. In v3, OUT is an empty `categories` array: in no defined category, NOT 'near the important one'. The old T1/T2/T3 hierarchy failed because 'adjacent' was defined by negation and OUT-vs-adjacent was the largest confusion at every sample size: the category was empty. T1 core metaresearch; T2 adjacent (STS, LIS, research infrastructure); T3 contextual (policy, editorials: mapped, never pooled with T1/T2); OUT otherwise. The in-scope decision that gates the corpus is tier in {T1, T2}. `insufficient_payload` (v2.1) is NOT a screening judgment: it states that the record cannot be screened at all (a scraping artifact as a title, boilerplate in the abstract field, a title and abstract from different papers, spam). It is distinct from OUT and must be REPORTED, not silently dropped: the size of this class is a finding about OpenAlex. Rubric v2.0 mandated this value while this enum could not express it, which is DEVIATIONS.md D20 committed by the document that fixes D20. See D25.

genre.description: OpenAlex `type` is unreliable and this field is commentary-heavy, so genre is screened rather than inherited.

about_ca.description: Is the work ABOUT the Canadian research system, irrespective of author location? This is the secondary estimand (PROTOCOL s3) and is recorded separately from the primary.

confidence.description: The screener's own confidence, as defined in the rubric. QUOTED VERBATIM from rubric v2: "if the abstract is missing, judge on the title alone and set confidence to `low` unless the title is unambiguous." In v1 this gloss PARAPHRASED the rubric as requiring `low` WHENEVER the abstract is missing, which is a different rule; since `low` routes a record to human adjudication and a third of the frame has no abstract, the paraphrase silently changed which records a human ever looks at (DEVIATIONS.md D24). A schema quotes its codebook; it never restates it.

reason.description: Optional. One clause naming the rubric criterion that decided it. Required when confidence is `low` or tier is T2 (the contested boundary).

domain.description: Which of Ioannidis's five meta-research domains the work belongs to. QUOTED from rubric v2.2, which quotes Ioannidis JPA, PLoS Biol 2018;16(3):e2005468: "Meta-research is the study of research itself: its methods, reporting, reproducibility, evaluation, and incentives." REQUIRED for T1 (the canonical corpus). null for T2/T3/OUT: T2 holds the adjacent traditions the call names by name (bibliometrics, STS, scholarly communication, open science), which are IN THE MAP but are not inside the canonical definition, and forcing them into one of the five would delete the traditions the inclusiveness criterion exists to protect.

categories.description: Every category a work belongs to; MAY BE MORE THAN ONE, and empty means OUT. Each is defined VERBATIM from its own literature in rubric v3, from a PDF in docs/reference/definitions/: metaresearch (Ioannidis 2015), metaepi_narrow (Murad 2017) and metaepi_broad (Kataoka 2023) which are CODED SEPARATELY because the definition is disputed in print (Puljak 2020, 175 sources, no consensus), bibliometrics (Mingers & Leydesdorff 2015), sts (Jasanoff 2004; Latour), scholarly_communication (Borgman 2007), open_science (UNESCO 2021), research_integrity (Fanelli 2009; COPE). The previous T1/T2/T3 hierarchy is RETIRED: 'adjacent' was defined by negation and OUT-vs-adjacent was the largest confusion at every sample size, because the category was empty. Categories are NOT ranked.
